brief.scope: Fresh recheck of the eight original interface findings after the four-document correction. Verify canonical launch identity, unique LaunchSelection type, full adapter/normalizer mapping and digest binding, explicit pending unit1a counterpart, read/live exits including cleanup-unreachable, all CLI forwarding forms and refusal example. Inspect producer machine-check receipt; independently execute available checks or state limits. No code/host/settings/authority changes, broad re-audit or new roadmap gates. Inline REVIEW <=1000 words, actual model/exact ref, approve/changes and precise remaining findings.

findings.claim: The correction closed the cleanup half of the exit gap and left the identity half open. Declared: "Report exit 0 requires every requested arm PASS, matching verified identities and cleanup complete. A completed report exits 1 when any row is FAIL or UNREACHABLE, or cleanup is `failed` or `unreachable`, including all-PASS rows with unobservable cleanup" (lines 292-296). Practiced elsewhere in the same frozen family: "Unavailable tuple members make identity null with an unreachable reason" (harness-capabilities.md:235) and the report field "identity | null if unavailable" (probes-lever.md:262). A completed report with every arm PASS, cleanup complete and identity null or non-matching is barred from exit 0 and is named by no exit-1 clause; exit 2 is reserved for pre-act malformed arguments or untrusted bootstrap transport (line 297-299), so a post-run identity mismatch has no declared exit class. This is the same defect shape as the cleanup-unreachable finding the change was asked to fix.

The producer's machine-check receipt is stamped to a version it does not describe. Declared: `"base": "8a788d5ecbd1720204fd0139f24a74394d05b6e6", "head": "8a788d5ecbd1720204fd0139f24a74394d05b6e6"`. Practiced: its files_sha256 are the corrected bytes (f96a9339..., cd09a68f..., f83fa7ae..., a6827d12...), which I reproduced against the snapshot at 8fd333e; at 8a788d5 those four files differ by the producer's own measurement, "76 insertions and 26 deletions" (ag-conduct-interface-fix.json, finding at "final tree and commit message"), which I confirmed as `git show --stat 8fd333e` = 4 files, 76 insertions(+), 26 deletions(-). The receipt also carries no checked_at date. Under verified-couplings obligation 4 a verification is true of one version on one day; this one names the wrong version and no day.

findings.claim: The landed commit message is garbled by trailer hoisting. The producer wrote Finder/Fixer/Validation as a body paragraph (ag-conduct-interface-fix.json, result.envelope.commit.body); git parsed `Validation: git diff --check; scratch machine checks of four JSON examples,` as a trailer and moved it into the trailer block, stranding its two continuation lines as an orphan paragraph that now opens mid-sentence: "34 local links/anchors, six adapter mappings, and nine cleanup exit states." The durable record therefore reads as a sentence fragment, and the trailer block holds a line that is a continuation, not a trailer. AGENTS.md requires `Source:` and `Co-Authored-By:` on every commit; both are present and correct, so this is message hygiene, not a missing trailer.

Three of the correction's edits were spliced into existing paragraphs without rewrapping, against the surrounding fill. conductor-start-plan.md:90 is the orphan line `the adapter` and line 92 runs to 127 columns ("are forwarded exactly, in order; rejected tokens never reach launch records. `test` exercises live harness enforcement; a profile"), joining the new forwarding sentence to the pre-existing `test` sentence in one line. probes-lever.md:155 and 329 are the same splice shape. The only other over-long lines in these files are pre-existing URL citations (conductor-start-plan.md:277-279), so the fill convention is otherwise held.

Scope. Fresh recheck of the eight findings from review 20260906T104703Z-review-claude-e076d5 after the four-document correction landed by 20260906T105714Z-code-codex-20b3d6. All three in/ files read whole. Commit 8fd333e touches exactly the four owned documents, 76 insertions and 26 deletions (git show --stat), matching the producer's claim; git diff --check over 710dbac..8fd333e exits 0 with no output.

The eight, one by one.

1 (p2, launch_id). Closed. conductor-start-plan.md:339-347 now defines DispatchID as the canonical execution record id under the dispatch job directory, `<UTC stamp>-<stage>-<harness>-<6 hex>`, states "It is not discovery's `ID`", and binds launch_id byte-for-byte with fresh reservation on launch and retention on resume. I confirmed the anchor `### The job directory` at CONTRACT.md:445 and the grammar verbatim at CONTRACT.md:469, and that the cited example `20260906T103421Z-code-codex-20aa14` is a real record in this branch. The descriptor-to-record edge is now declared.

2 (Selection collision). Closed. `LaunchSelection` is defined once at conductor-start-plan.md:349-352 and explicitly distinguished from discovery's handoff `Selection`. grep over the four documents plus discovery-lever.md shows no ambiguous bare `Selection` cite remains: the three consumers now read LaunchSelection (harness-capabilities.md:90, 210; probes-lever.md:260, 328).

3 (Abort contradiction). Closed. probes-lever.md:149-155 scopes the Exits section to the read-only `probes.py` run/ask/grade verbs, says those verbs do not produce Abort, and forwards live-diagnostic exits including Abort (3) to #live-observation-format, which resolves.

4 (adapter mapping, normalizer digest). Closed. Descriptor adapter is now six fields including mechanism and normalizer_sha256 (line 361); the identity adapter is five (harness-capabilities.md:213); the new table at 245-252 maps all six descriptor fields, routing executable_sha256 to harness.executable.sha256, and states the consequence that the Request binding digest and the compiled invariant digest cover the pinned normalizer and mechanism. Both closed objects are covered completely in both directions.

5 (evaluate_tool dangling). Closed as a declared absence, which is the correct remedy under docs/wire.md. permission-surface.md:95-99 names adoption unit 1a as the owner of the matching declaration and calls it "a declared unresolved edge". I re-measured: lane-policy.md still contains no evaluate_tool, only the module home at line 417.

6 (cleanup=unreachable). Closed for cleanup. probes-lever.md:293-296 sends `failed` or `unreachable` cleanup to exit 1, "including all-PASS rows with unobservable cleanup", and keeps unreachable as unavailable evidence rather than observed failure. See finding 1 in findings[] for the identity condition in the same sentence, which was not closed.

7 (CLI forwarding). Closed in substance. All four synopsis forms carry `[-- <adapter-token>...]`, and lines 85-92 state that `--` follows all conduct positionals including `test`, may have zero following tokens, and that forwarding is admitted on all four forms. The wrap of that edit is finding 5.

8 (semicolon in a fixed refusal field). Closed. permission-surface.md:150-154 adds the rule that fixed field values contain no semicolon and the example needed is now "use canonical dispatch and run the independent doctor for gate diagnosis". The two other new refusal templates (conduct-argv at harness-capabilities.md:177, conduct-mcp at conductor-start-plan.md:429) are also semicolon-free inside their fields.

Checks I executed. sha256sum on the four documents reproduces the receipt's files_sha256 exactly, so the receipt describes the bytes under review. json_examples=4 and local_links=34 recomputed and matched. All 34 local links resolve: thirteen distinct file targets exist (ls) and all ten distinct anchors resolve to real headings, verified by heading grep in conductor-start-plan.md, harness-capabilities.md, permission-surface.md, probes-lever.md, lane-policy.md:390, discovery-lever.md:57, CONTRACT.md:218 and CONTRACT.md:445. adapter_mapping (6) and cleanup_exit_matrix (9, PASS/unreachable → 1) match the text. The refusal_wire string matches the serialized Decision example. Two receipt claims did not reproduce; they are findings 2 and 3.

Limits, declared. The ten loopstrap remote links are historical and were not fetched — no network in this profile. I could not execute a shell script from out/ (bash script invocation refused), so the link/anchor check was done by per-target ls and heading grep instead; out/linkcheck.sh is left unrun and is labelled as such in artifacts. awk and `git -C` were refused; `git log`, `git show` and `git diff --check` ran. The producer's scratch checker was not supplied, so its internal counts could not be re-executed, only compared against the documents. No repository, test, settings or host write, no vendor launch, no probe or suite run. Nothing here admits a harness, activates policy, or reopens accepted discovery, C1/C2 or lane-policy architecture.
